title: `SeparationRayShape2D` resolves penetration without accounting for motion
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1] ### System information Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8129) - AMD Ryzen 7 7745HX with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 63.18 GiB memory ### Issue description By default, `SeparationRayShape2D` disregards the motion of it's body when resolving collisions. This is due to `GodotSpace2D::test_body_motion` skipping step 2 (motion collision) for `SeparationRayShape2D`. This results in penetration only being resolved on the frame after it happens. In many cases this results in a single frame where the body that has the `SeparationRayShape2D` visibly sinking into walls/floors/etc. When a constant large velocity is applied to the body, this results in a constant penetration of the body. What seems to be happening is thus: 1. Frame starts 1. Body checks for collisions but finds none as `SeparationRayShape2D` doesn't check along motion 1. Body moves and now overlaps 1. Frame ends and displays body overlapping 1. Frame starts 1. Body checks for collisions and finds the overlap 1. Body resolves collision 1. Body moves and now overlaps again. 1. Frame ends and displays body overlapping The expected behavior it that the depenetration step should move the `SeparationRayShape2D` out of collision entirely regardless of velocity. While this is technically resolved by setting `slide_on_slope` to `true` for the `SeparationRayShape2D`, this behavior is not indicated in the documentation (plus it isn't intuitive). Incapsulates #77571 ### Steps to reproduce All that is necessary is to have a `CharacterBody2D` with a `SeparationRayShape2D`. It will be more apparent the larger the velocity and the more parallel the `SeparationRayShape2D` and collision normal are. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [example.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22973066/example.zip) Enable Debug -> Visible Collision Shapes Contains a `CharacterBody2D` plus a `RigidBody2D` for reference. Press space to apply a constant velocity to the `CharacterBody2D`
